student_answer: Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) is the algorithm used to train recurrent neural networks. It works by conceptually unrolling the recurrent network over the sequence length T into a deep feedforward computational graph with tied weights. student_answer: BPTT extends reverse-mode automatic differentiation to recurrent computational graphs. Given a sequence of length T with total loss L = sum_{t=1}^T L_t, the RNN is unrolled into an equivalent feedforward graph where weight matrices W are shared across all T time steps. Applying the chain rule yields dL/dW = sum_{t=1}^T dL_t/dW, where each dL_t/dW expands into a temporal chain sum_{k=1}^t (dL_t/dh_t) * (prod_{j=k+1}^t dh_j/dh_{j-1}) * (dh_k/dW). Gradients are accumulated across all unrolled steps to update the tied parameters.
